steps.label: Anointed in secret
steps.copy: At Ramoth-gilead, a young prophet sent by Elisha pours oil on Jehu's head in an inner room and runs off.

steps.label: Riding to Jezreel
steps.copy: Jehu mounts his chariot and rides to Jezreel, where King Joram is recovering from his wounds.

steps.label: “Driving like a madman”
steps.copy: The watchman reports: “He is driving like a madman!”

steps.label: Joram struck down
steps.copy: They meet at Naboth's field. Jehu draws his bow and shoots Joram between the shoulders.

steps.label: Jezebel's end
steps.copy: Jezebel is thrown down from a window, as the Lord had spoken through Elijah.

set.note: Where the Assyrian camp was when it was struck isn't said. The king had moved on from Lachish to fight Libnah (2 Kings 19:8).

steps.label: Tribute to Lachish
steps.copy: Hezekiah sends silver and gold to the king of Assyria at Lachish.

steps.label: The army at the wall
steps.copy: A great force comes up from Lachish and stands by the conduit of the upper pool, mocking Judah's trust in the Lord.

steps.label: The letter spread out
steps.copy: Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before the Lord and prays.

steps.label: The camp struck
steps.copy: That night the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh.

steps.label: Toward Egypt
steps.copy: After Gedaliah is murdered, Johanan leads the survivors from Mizpah to Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, afraid of Babylon.

steps.label: Ask the Lord
steps.copy: They beg Jeremiah to pray. The answer: stay in the land, and do not go to Egypt.

steps.label: Refusing the word
steps.copy: They call it a lie and take the whole remnant, Jeremiah and Baruch too, into Egypt as far as Tahpanhes.

steps.label: Stones in the pavement
steps.copy: Jeremiah buries large stones at Pharaoh's palace: Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne over them.

set.note: Tarshish lay far to the west, often linked with Tartessus in Spain; the ship never got there. Where the storm struck is not recorded.

steps.label: Down to Joppa
steps.copy: Told to go to Nineveh, Jonah runs the other way. At Joppa he pays the fare for a ship bound for Tarshish.

steps.label: The great storm
steps.copy: The Lord hurls a great wind on the sea, and the ship is about to break apart. Jonah sleeps below.

steps.label: The lot falls on Jonah
steps.copy: The sailors cast lots, and Jonah tells them to throw him into the sea.

steps.label: Cast into the sea
steps.copy: They throw him overboard and the sea grows calm.

steps.label: The great fish
steps.copy: The Lord appoints a great fish to swallow Jonah, and he is inside it three days and three nights.

set.note: Daniel doesn't record the road. Travelers usually went north around the desert, roughly 900 miles.

steps.label: Jerusalem besieged
steps.copy: In the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar comes against Jerusalem and besieges it.

steps.label: Vessels to Shinar
steps.copy: The Lord gives Jehoiakim into his hand, and he carries temple vessels to the land of Shinar.

steps.label: Chosen youths
steps.copy: Young men of Israel's royal and noble families are chosen to learn the language and literature of the Chaldeans.

steps.label: Daniel among them
steps.copy: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah are among them, and they are given new names.

steps.label: A call to war
steps.copy: At Samaria, Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.

steps.label: Micaiah's vision
steps.copy: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd.”

steps.label: Up to battle
steps.copy: The two kings go up to Ramoth-gilead, Ahab in disguise.

steps.label: A random arrow
steps.copy: A man draws his bow at random and hits the king between the joints of his armor. He dies that evening.

steps.label: Brought to Samaria
steps.copy: He is buried in Samaria, and dogs lick up his blood at the pool, as the Lord had said.

set.note: Genesis says people journeyed eastward and settled on a plain in Shinar (Babylonia). The city is called Babel.

steps.label: Settling in Shinar
steps.copy: The whole world has one language. Journeying eastward, people find a plain in Shinar and settle there.

steps.label: A tower to the heavens
steps.copy: “Let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens.”

steps.label: Languages confused
steps.copy: The Lord comes down and confuses their language so they cannot understand one another.

steps.label: Scattered abroad
steps.copy: The Lord scatters them over all the earth, and the city is called Babel.

steps.label: Toward the Negev
steps.copy: Abraham moves into the Negev, between Kadesh and Shur, and stays for a time in Gerar.

steps.label: Sarah taken
steps.copy: Abraham says of Sarah, “She is my sister,” and Abimelech king of Gerar has her brought to him.

steps.label: A dream of warning
steps.copy: God comes to Abimelech in a dream: “You are as good as dead,” for she is a married woman.

steps.label: Healing through prayer
steps.copy: Abimelech returns Sarah. Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech and his household.

steps.label: Sent into the wild
steps.copy: Abraham gives Hagar bread and a skin of water and sends her off with the boy. She wanders in the wilderness of Beersheba.

steps.label: A mother's grief
steps.copy: When the water is gone, she puts the boy under a bush and sits away from him, weeping.

steps.label: God hears the boy
steps.copy: “Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.”

steps.label: A well revealed
steps.copy: God opens her eyes, and she sees a well of water.

steps.label: Home in Paran
steps.copy: God is with the boy. He becomes an archer and lives in the wilderness of Paran.

steps.label: Leaving Jacob
steps.copy: Esau takes his family and livestock to a land away from Jacob; the land cannot support them both.

steps.label: Dwelling in Seir
steps.copy: Esau, that is Edom, settles in the hill country of Seir.

steps.label: Father of Edom
steps.copy: These are the generations of Esau, father of the Edomites.

steps.label: Chiefs of Edom
steps.copy: The chiefs of Edom are listed by their places in the land they possess.

set.note: The camps after Sinai (Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah, Hazeroth) are unknown sites; the first stop is placed roughly three days on.

steps.label: The cloud lifts
steps.copy: In the second year the cloud rises from the tabernacle, and Israel sets out from the wilderness of Sinai.

steps.label: Tribe by tribe
steps.copy: They march in order under their banners, Judah first.

steps.label: The ark leads
steps.copy: The ark goes ahead of them three days to find a place to rest, the cloud over them by day.

steps.label: “Rise up, O LORD!”
steps.copy: Whenever the ark set out, Moses said, “Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered.”

steps.label: Into Paran
steps.copy: After Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah and Hazeroth, they camp in the wilderness of Paran.

set.note: Kibroth-hattaavah is unknown. Hazeroth is traditionally placed at Ain Hudhera.

steps.label: Craving meat
steps.copy: The people weep again: “Who will feed us meat?” They remember the fish of Egypt.

steps.label: Quail from the sea
steps.copy: A wind from the Lord drives quail in from the sea all around the camp.

steps.label: Graves of craving
steps.copy: A plague strikes, and the place is named Kibroth-hattaavah, where they bury the people who craved.

steps.label: On to Hazeroth
steps.copy: From there the people journey to Hazeroth and stay there.

set.note: Numbers doesn't say where the battle was fought; the Midianites were then living alongside Moab (Numbers 22:4; 25:6).

steps.label: Called to war
steps.copy: Moses says, “Arm some of your men for war,” a thousand from each tribe, with Phinehas the priest.

steps.label: Midian defeated
steps.copy: They fight against Midian and kill its five kings and Balaam son of Beor.

steps.label: Back to the camp
steps.copy: They bring the captives and plunder to Moses and Eleazar at the camp on the plains of Moab.

steps.label: Good land for cattle
steps.copy: Reuben and Gad have huge herds and see that Jazer and Gilead are good for livestock.

steps.label: A bold request
steps.copy: “Let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.” Moses warns them.

steps.label: Armed and ready
steps.copy: They promise to cross over armed ahead of Israel until every tribe has its land.

steps.label: Granted
steps.copy: Moses gives them, with half of Manasseh, the kingdoms of Sihon and Og.

steps.label: Building cities
steps.copy: The Gadites build Dibon, Ataroth and Aroer; the Reubenites rebuild Heshbon and others.

steps.label: Gilead taken
steps.copy: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh take Gilead and settle there.

steps.label: A cunning plan
steps.copy: The Gibeonites load worn-out sacks, old patched wineskins and dry, moldy bread.

steps.label: Coming to Gilgal
steps.copy: “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”

steps.label: Peace sworn
steps.copy: Without asking the Lord, Joshua makes peace with them, and the leaders swear an oath.

steps.label: Neighbors after all
steps.copy: Three days later Israel learns they are neighbors and reaches their cities on the third day.

steps.label: Woodcutters and water carriers
steps.copy: Bound by the oath, Israel spares them, and they serve the house of God.

steps.label: Coming to Joshua
steps.copy: At Gilgal, Caleb reminds Joshua of the Lord's promise at Kadesh-barnea, forty-five years before.

steps.label: “Give me this hill country”
steps.copy: At eighty-five he asks for the hill country where the Anakim live.

steps.label: Hebron granted
steps.copy: Joshua blesses Caleb and gives him Hebron, because he followed the Lord fully.

steps.label: The Anakim driven out
steps.copy: Caleb drives out the three sons of Anak from Hebron.

steps.label: Debir taken
steps.copy: Othniel captures Debir and wins Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife.

steps.label: Israel gathered
steps.copy: Joshua gathers all the tribes at Shechem and retells all the Lord has done.

steps.label: “Choose this day”
steps.copy: “As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!”

steps.label: A covenant made
steps.copy: Joshua makes a covenant for the people that day at Shechem.

steps.label: The witness stone
steps.copy: He sets up a large stone under the oak near the sanctuary of the Lord.

steps.label: Joshua buried
steps.copy: Joshua dies at 110 and is buried in his inheritance at Timnath-serah.

steps.label: Joseph's bones
steps.copy: The bones of Joseph, brought up from Egypt, are buried at Shechem on the land Jacob bought.

steps.label: Going to Bethlehem
steps.copy: In the days with no king, a Levite from Ephraim goes to Bethlehem to bring back his concubine.

steps.label: Lingering
steps.copy: Her father keeps them for days; late on the fifth day they finally set out.

steps.label: Passing Jebus
steps.copy: They will not stop in Jebus, a city of foreigners.

steps.label: Lodging at Gibeah
steps.copy: At sunset they reach Gibeah of Benjamin, and an old man takes them in.

steps.label: Israel roused
steps.copy: After a night of violence there, the Levite sends word through all Israel: “Nothing like this has been seen or done.”
